content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks under the project's tsconfig. The only errors left are in `src/module.ts`, which still imports lodash, and lodash isn't installed here. I couldn't compare results against the original lodash functions for the same reason. I ran `npm run size -- out/module.ts`: it printed 2287 bytes (min+gzip), with 85 bytes of my own code. The original's size couldn't be measured, since lodash isn't installed.

| Function | Replacement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `merge` | `merge` from `es-toolkit` | It mutates `base` and merges arrays by index, as lodash does. Within the stated input range, I expect the same results. |
| `startCase` | `startCase` from `es-toolkit/compat` | The strict version doesn't match lodash when capitals run together. `ABCdef9x` gives `Ab Cdef 9 X` there, against `AB Cdef 9 X` from compat. The input range includes consecutive capitals, so I used compat. |
| `isEmpty` | `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat` | The strict package has no `isEmpty`. |

The strict `startCase` would have been much smaller, at 880 bytes. I chose compat anyway because the output has to match the original.

No lodash import remains, and I added no adapters or hand-written replacements. The exported signatures, `Row` and `Config` are unchanged.
